title: SKP Processor
description: Processor replicas. service_name is a real multi-select here: a processor takes its name and version from its database row via the two-stage boot, so different images carry different identities.

panels.title: Gate open
panels.description: Measures `pipeline.gate.open`, minimum across replicas. 1 = the projection store is usable and consumers may run; 0 = the gate is shut and every delivery is being requeued.

panels.title: Identity ready
panels.description: 0 means the pod is up and waiting for a processor row whose SourceHash matches its image. Running / NotReady with 0 restarts is the designed behaviour, not a crash loop -- this is the metric that makes that legible.

panels.title: Not acked
panels.description:
Measures `pipeline.messages.consumed` with disposition requeued or parked, over the last 5m. Split by `reason` on `Messages consumed by disposition`.

A redelivery counts twice, by design: a delivery whose ack the broker never heard comes back and increments again.

targets.expr: ((sum(increase(pipeline_messages_consumed_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",processorId=~"$processorId",disposition=~"requeued|parked"}[5m])) or vector(0)) > (clamp_min((sum(pipeline_messages_consumed_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",processorId=~"$processorId",disposition=~"requeued|parked"}) or vector(0)) - (sum(pipeline_messages_consumed_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",processorId=~"$processorId",disposition=~"requeued|parked"} offset 5m) or vector(0)), 0))) or (clamp_min((sum(pipeline_messages_consumed_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",processorId=~"$processorId",disposition=~"requeued|parked"}) or vector(0)) - (sum(pipeline_messages_consumed_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",processorId=~"$processorId",disposition=~"requeued|parked"} offset 5m) or vector(0)), 0))

panels.title: Produce faults
panels.description:
Measures `pipeline.messages.produced` with outcome transient, unroutable or refused, over the last 5m.

unroutable = the queue is not declared. transient = the broker is unreachable. Opposite remedies, which is why the outcome is a tag.

targets.expr: ((sum(increase(pipeline_messages_produced_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",processorId=~"$processorId",outcome=~"transient|unroutable|refused"}[5m])) or vector(0)) > (clamp_min((sum(pipeline_messages_produced_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",processorId=~"$processorId",outcome=~"transient|unroutable|refused"}) or vector(0)) - (sum(pipeline_messages_produced_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",processorId=~"$processorId",outcome=~"transient|unroutable|refused"} offset 5m) or vector(0)), 0))) or (clamp_min((sum(pipeline_messages_produced_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",processorId=~"$processorId",outcome=~"transient|unroutable|refused"}) or vector(0)) - (sum(pipeline_messages_produced_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",processorId=~"$processorId",outcome=~"transient|unroutable|refused"} offset 5m) or vector(0)), 0))

panels.title: Not acked (range)
panels.description:
Measures `pipeline.messages.consumed` with disposition requeued or parked, over the visible range.

The Verdict tier's `Not acked` is the same instrument over the last 5m.

targets.expr: ((sum(increase(pipeline_messages_consumed_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",processorId=~"$processorId",disposition=~"requeued|parked"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) > (clamp_min((sum(pipeline_messages_consumed_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",processorId=~"$processorId",disposition=~"requeued|parked"}) or vector(0)) - (sum(pipeline_messages_consumed_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",processorId=~"$processorId",disposition=~"requeued|parked"} offset $__range) or vector(0)), 0))) or (clamp_min((sum(pipeline_messages_consumed_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",processorId=~"$processorId",disposition=~"requeued|parked"}) or vector(0)) - (sum(pipeline_messages_consumed_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",processorId=~"$processorId",disposition=~"requeued|parked"} offset $__range) or vector(0)), 0))

panels.title: Produce faults (range)
panels.description:
Measures `pipeline.messages.produced` with a non-accepted outcome, over the visible range.

`(range)` is what separates it from the Verdict tier's `Produce faults`, which reads the same instrument over the last 5m. Same question, two tenses -- without the qualifier the board carries two panels under one title.

targets.expr: ((sum(increase(pipeline_messages_produced_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",processorId=~"$processorId",outcome=~"transient|unroutable|refused"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) > (clamp_min((sum(pipeline_messages_produced_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",processorId=~"$processorId",outcome=~"transient|unroutable|refused"}) or vector(0)) - (sum(pipeline_messages_produced_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",processorId=~"$processorId",outcome=~"transient|unroutable|refused"} offset $__range) or vector(0)), 0))) or (clamp_min((sum(pipeline_messages_produced_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",processorId=~"$processorId",outcome=~"transient|unroutable|refused"}) or vector(0)) - (sum(pipeline_messages_produced_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",processorId=~"$processorId",outcome=~"transient|unroutable|refused"} offset $__range) or vector(0)), 0))

panels.title: Dead-letter depth (all queues)
panels.description:
Measures `pipeline.deadletter.depth`, summed across this service's dead-letter queues, right now.

A level, not a count of events: it falls when someone drains the queue. Should be 0; anything else is work that lost progress permanently.

panels.title: Restarts
panels.description:
Measures `changes(pipeline.process.start.timestamp)` across replicas over the visible range. The gauge holds the process start time and moves exactly once per process.

`max`, not `sum`: this answers *did anything restart*. It sees an in-place container restart, because InstanceId is the pod name and the value moves on an existing series; a rollout that REPLACES the pod starts a new series instead.

panels.title: Produced by type and outcome
panels.description: Egress. outcome != accepted is a fault.

panels.title: Messages consumed by disposition
panels.description:
Measures the rate of `pipeline.messages.consumed` by queue and disposition. Exactly one increment per delivery, on every exit path.

**Grouped exactly like `Consumer duration by disposition` so the two read together** -- same keys, same legend order, one panel giving the rate of each path and the other its cost. They were split differently before, which made a single collapsed line here look like twice the volume of a neighbour that split the same total across more series.

All three dispositions are seeded, so a path flat at zero is a quiet path rather than an unmeasured one. **`reason` is no longer a dimension here**, and that is a real loss: it is what separated the four causes behind `requeued`, and during a store outage `gate_closed` floods the same line that `send_failed` and `escaped` arrive on. Split by `reason` in Explore when triaging a requeue spike.

targets.expr: (sum by (queue,disposition) (rate(pipeline_messages_consumed_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",processorId=~"$processorId"}[$__rate_interval]))) or (label_replace(group by (queue) (last_over_time(pipeline_messages_consumed_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",processorId=~"$processorId"}[$__range])), "disposition", "acked", "", "") * 0) or (label_replace(group by (queue) (last_over_time(pipeline_messages_consumed_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",processorId=~"$processorId"}[$__range])), "disposition", "requeued", "", "") * 0) or (label_replace(group by (queue) (last_over_time(pipeline_messages_consumed_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",processorId=~"$processorId"}[$__range])), "disposition", "parked", "", "") * 0)

panels.title: Produce duration
panels.description:
Measures `pipeline.produce.duration` by destination — from the start of a send until the broker confirmed or refused it, publisher confirm included. p95, p99 and mean.

Read the mean: at this sample rate the quantiles interpolate between bucket edges and flip between rungs rather than moving.

panels.title: Gate probe outcomes
panels.description:
Measures the RATE of `pipeline.gate.probe.duration` observations, split by outcome — healthy, timeout or failed.

Probe attempts per second, not gate state. The gate's own posture is `Gate open`; this is what the probe found each time it asked.

panels.title: Gate probe duration
panels.description:
Measures `pipeline.gate.probe.duration` — how long the projection store took to answer the gate probe. p95, p99 and mean.

All three read `outcome="healthy"` only. A timed-out probe records the ceiling rather than a latency and would pin p99 at exactly the probe timeout; those are counted on `Gate probe outcomes` instead.

panels.title: Dead-letter depth by queue
panels.description:
Measures `pipeline.deadletter.depth` per queue — refused messages nobody has dealt with yet.

A level, not a rate: it steps up on a park and falls only when someone drains the queue. Read on the park event rather than waiting for the 5-minute poll.

defaults.noValue: no dead-letter depth reported by this service -- see the panel description before reading this as zero

panels.title: Gate open and trips by replica
panels.description:
Measures `pipeline.gate.open` per replica, with `increase(pipeline.gate.trips)` over the range beside it.

The counter is what sees a fault that HEALED: a trip that shut the gate and reopened it leaves the gauge back at 1 with nothing to show. An absent trips series means never tripped — that counter is unseeded, so it has no series until the first trip.

defaults.noValue: no gate reporting -- this replica is not exporting at all

panels.title: Identity ready by replica
panels.description:
Measures `pipeline.identity.ready` per replica. Red is a pod that is up and waiting for a processor row matching its SourceHash — the designed behaviour, not a crash loop.

A row that ENDS is a replica that left. Departed replicas linger for one liveness window, which is why this is a state timeline and not a filled area.

panels.title: Queue depth by queue
panels.description:
Measures `pipeline.queue.depth` per queue — messages ready and not yet taken, from the broker's own passive declare.

The only leading indicator on this board: a queue fills as soon as a consumer is merely SLOWER than its producer. Healthy here is 0 on orchestrator queues and mean 0.65 / max 3 on the work queue, where prefetch 1 drains a cron batch one message at a time.

defaults.noValue: no queue depth reported -- nothing is probing these queues

panels.title: Consumers attached by queue
panels.description:
Measures `pipeline.queue.consumers` per queue — how many consumers THE BROKER has attached. 0 means nothing is listening.

Expect 2 on the processor work queue. Wrapped in a 40s liveness window: unwrapped, a departed pod's stale series read a confident 2 against the broker's 0 for a whole outage.

defaults.noValue: no consumer count reported -- nothing is probing these queues

panels.title: Messages consumed by replica
panels.description:
Measures the rate of acked `pipeline.messages.consumed` per replica. Replicas share one queue and the broker round-robins, so a replica near zero beside working peers is consuming nothing while still looking healthy.

Gated on identity liveness, so a departed replica's line ENDS at its true last rate instead of decaying with the range.

panels.title: Loop iterations by loop
panels.description:
Measures the rate of `pipeline.loop.iterations` by loop. Expected: l2-gate 0.2/s, processor-liveness and queue-depth 0.1/s.

The counter is seeded with Add(0) per loop at startup, so 0 means the loop stopped. An EMPTY panel means the process is not reporting at all.

panels.title: Consumer duration by disposition
panels.description:
Measures `pipeline.consumer.duration` — how long a delivery was held, on every exit path including the ones that never reached a handler.

All three dispositions are seeded, so a flat zero is a path nothing took, not a fast one; `Messages consumed by disposition` tells them apart. A mean rather than a quantile, because at this sample rate quantiles interpolate.

targets.expr: (sum by (queue,disposition) (rate(pipeline_consumer_duration_seconds_sum{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",processorId=~"$processorId"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (queue,disposition) (rate(pipeline_consumer_duration_seconds_count{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",processorId=~"$processorId"}[$__rate_interval]))) or (label_replace(group by (queue) (last_over_time(pipeline_consumer_duration_seconds_count{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",processorId=~"$processorId"}[$__range])), "disposition", "acked", "", "") * 0) or (label_replace(group by (queue) (last_over_time(pipeline_consumer_duration_seconds_count{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",processorId=~"$processorId"}[$__range])), "disposition", "requeued", "", "") * 0) or (label_replace(group by (queue) (last_over_time(pipeline_consumer_duration_seconds_count{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",processorId=~"$processorId"}[$__range])), "disposition", "parked", "", "") * 0)

panels.title: Queue wait by queue
panels.description:
Measures `pipeline.queue.wait` — seconds between a message being published and a consumer picking it up, as a mean by queue.

`raw` double-counts the sender's own publisher confirm: the header is stamped before the publish, so ~12 of ~13ms sits in both this and `pipeline.produce.duration`. `net` subtracts the produce mean for the same destination and is the true broker wait.

targets.expr: avg by (queue) (rate(pipeline_queue_wait_seconds_sum{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",processorId=~"$processorId"}[$__rate_interval]) / rate(pipeline_queue_wait_seconds_count{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",processorId=~"$processorId"}[$__rate_interval])) - on(queue) group_left avg by (queue) (label_replace(rate(pipeline_produce_duration_seconds_sum{destination=~"processor-$processorId"}[$__rate_interval]) / rate(pipeline_produce_duration_seconds_count{destination=~"processor-$processorId"}[$__rate_interval]), "queue", "$1", "destination", "(.*)"))

defaults.noValue: no deliveries carrying a send timestamp in range

panels.title: Exception rate
panels.description: Correlates with rising parked / refused dispositions and with faulted process outcomes. On the visible tier because a rising exception rate is a cause an operator should not have to expand a row to find.

panels.title: Thread-pool queue length
panels.description: Explains consumption stalling while the gate is open and the consumer still reports consuming=1: callbacks are starved, not blocked.

panels.title: Thread-pool threads
panels.description:
Measures `process_runtime_dotnet_thread_pool_threads_count` per replica.

Read beside the queue length: a queue rising while this stays FLAT is starvation; rising while this CLIMBS is the pool injecting and merely lagging arrivals. At prefetch 1, one blocked callback is one idle replica.

panels.title: GC pause time
panels.description: Seconds of GC pause per second. Explains duration p99 spikes with no broker or dependency fault.

panels.title: GC collections / sec by generation
panels.description:
**The cause behind the pause time to its left.** Pause seconds answer *how much*, this answers *why*: gen0 is cheap and constant, and a gen2 rate that is anything but near-flat is the collection that actually costs you.

Split by generation rather than summed, because a summed collection rate is dominated by gen0 and moves for reasons that never cost a millisecond.

panels.title: GC heap size by generation
panels.description:
Managed heap, by generation. **The leak signal**: a gen2 or LOH line that steps up and never comes back down across several collections is retention, and it ends in an OOMKill that every pipeline panel will report as a restart with no cause.

By generation rather than a single total, because a rising total is normal between collections and says nothing; a rising gen2 FLOOR is the part that does not come back.

panels.title: GC committed memory
panels.description:
What the GC has committed from the OS -- **the number the container limit is compared against**, not the managed heap beside it. The two diverge, and the gap is why a pod can be OOMKilled while its heap looks healthy: committed memory is returned to the OS lazily, so it tracks the high-water mark rather than the live set.

Read this against the pod's memory limit; read the heap panel for whether the growth is real retention.

panels.title: Allocation rate
panels.description:
Bytes allocated per second -- **upstream of every other panel in this row.** Collections, pause time and committed memory are all consequences of this number; it is the one that moves first when a transform starts allocating per message.

Expect it to track the consumed rate. Allocation climbing while `Consumer paths` stays flat means the cost per message grew, which is a code change rather than a load change.

panels.title: Lock contention rate
panels.description:
Monitor contentions per second: threads that had to WAIT for a lock rather than take it. **The stall with no external cause** -- gate open, broker healthy, store fast, and throughput down anyway.

It earns a place on a processor board specifically because the concrete processor is a SINGLETON with per-dispatch state in plain fields, safe only because prefetch is 1. Contention here is the first sign that an author's transform introduced sharing the seam's design does not expect.
